setup_notes: Fork main was already up to date with upstream (ff + push no-op). No --stats flag in this tree; stage timings measured with the debug build's --trace and a small trace-summing script (phases.py).

hypotheses.title: Opaque langlib calls (push/clone/indexOf/map:get...) are re-monomorphized in every function body, each miss taking global write locks
hypotheses.issue: Calls to generic ('opaque') langlib functions (array:push, indexOf, map, remove, removeAll, toStream, value:clone, map:get, map:remove, xml ones) go through resolveOpaqueCallArgs -> opaque.FunctionDefinition.Monomorphize. The monomorphization cache lives in opaque.Context, which is created lazily PER RESOLVER (packageTypeResolver.opaqueContext / functionTypeResolver.opaqueContext), so every function body and lambda starts with an empty cache and re-materializes identical instantiations (e.g. int[] push) once per function instead of once per distinct instantiation. Each miss runs materializeOpaqueFn: re-runs the monomorphizer's subtype checks (cloneMonomorphizer -> IsSubtype), creates a new FunctionSymbol with a fmt.Sprintf name, builds a new function semtype (typeFromFunctionSignature -> opaque.FunctionSemType: list/function definitions + env atom interning), appends the symbol to the langlib module's shared SymbolSpace under its write lock (model/symbol.go SymbolSpace.AppendSymbol) and calls functionsignatures.(*Store).Associate under the single global Store.mu write lock. Since stage 5 runs function bodies concurrently across modules, these global write locks serialize it (mutex profile: ~88% of all wait in Store.Associate, ~11% in AppendSymbol, all under materializeOpaqueFn; same top mutex site on corpus/bench/10-bench/expressions-v.bal), the langlib symbol space grows by one symbol per call site per function, and Local Type Resolution gets SLOWER with more cores (mono 1107ms at GOMAXPROCS=1 vs 1232ms at 4, while a non-generic control speeds up 727->305ms). Pitfall for the fix: a naive shared cache keyed by SemTypeInterner handles gets almost no cross-function hits, because each type descriptor (e.g. every `int[]`) builds its own atoms and the interner compares BDD atoms by identity; the key must be compared structurally (or type descriptors' atoms must be canonicalized/interned).

hypotheses.fix_approach: Prototype adds a per-module, mutex-guarded opaque.MonoCache created in newPackageTypeResolver and passed into every resolver's opaque.Context. lookupMono first checks the existing lock-free per-resolver trie; on a miss it computes a structural hash of the cache keys (new semtypes.ShapeHash, depth-bounded walk over BDD atoms' atomic types ignoring atom identity) to select a bucket keyed by (owner, hash), and confirms candidates with new semtypes.IsSameShape (structural bisimulation over list/mapping/function/cell atomic types, resolving rec atoms through the context; conservative false for anything it does not compare). A hit is also stored in the local trie. storeMono writes local + appends to the shared bucket (append-only, so slices read after unlocking stay valid). Pitfalls: (1) interner-handle keys never match across function bodies because atoms are per-descriptor; (2) IsSameType matching works but costs ~20us per lookup and could attach a differently-printed equivalent type; (3) a single candidate list per owner went quadratic with 2000 distinct record instantiations (260ms -> 8.4s), fixed by hash bucketing; (4) bucketing by semtypes.ToString is too slow. Races where two bodies materialize the same instantiation simultaneously are harmless (an extra unused symbol, as ephemeral trials already create). Diagnostics stay per call site since only successful monomorphizations are cached. A cleaner production fix may be to canonicalize/intern atoms of type descriptors so identity-keyed caching works, or a module-level cache keyed by a canonical type key. make test and make test-race pass.

notes: Side observations from exploration (not pursued): stage 6 validatePackage runs sequentially within a module (~1.0-1.35 s on expressions-v, does not scale with cores); each nested loop wraps the resolver in another loopTypeResolver whose methods delegate up the chain (nested foreach depth 800 -> 2.3 s); `while` blocks nested 400+ deep panic in diagnostics with a negative start offset (possible bug worth a separate look).
